operations.source_name: Environment Agency LIDAR Time Stamped Point Cloud
operations.details_summary: EA documents an archive of time-stamped three-dimensional x,y,z LIDAR points and attributes from which site-specific DSM and DTM products are derived.

operations.source_name: Environment Agency LIDAR Time Stamped Point Cloud
operations.details_summary: Point-cloud returns are classified into ground and surface-object classes; surface-object returns are not accepted as bare-earth parcel relief.

operations.source_name: Environment Agency LIDAR Time Stamped Point Cloud
operations.details_summary: EA states manual editing of the derived DTM means classified ground points need not match the final DTM; raw ground classes therefore cannot silently replace the SHA-bound DTM result.

operations.source_name: Environment Agency LIDAR Time Stamped Point Cloud
operations.details_summary: EA notes that historic archiving means a matching point cloud may not exist for every derived surface model; absence of a matching point cloud is not treated as evidence for substituting another survey.

operations.source_name: Environment Agency LIDAR Time Stamped Point Cloud
operations.details_summary: Official point-cloud metadata declares EPSG:27700; parcel metric geometry remains in British National Grid rather than a web-display projection.

operations.source_name: Environment Agency LIDAR Time Stamped Point Cloud
operations.details_summary: EA gives the LIDAR dataset vertical accuracy as +/-15 cm RMSE; this remains a dataset-level error contract and is not converted into an invented parcel-specific precision.
The official 10 m DTM is retained as a negative-resolution control, not as an accuracy upgrade over the 1 m primary source.
EA states the 10 m DTM is resampled from the 2 m DTM using bilinear interpolation; it is therefore rejected as a precision upgrade for parcel-scale relief.
The 10 m product is aligned to the OS National Grid, in metres, referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn and uses OSTN15; datum compatibility alone does not make its coarse grid preferable.
The +/-15 cm source-survey RMSE is not interpreted as a claim that a bilinearly resampled 10 m grid preserves 1 m parcel-scale spatial detail.
Row 30762 remains 0.270 m at 96% result confidence; point-cloud and coarse-grid controls justify no numeric mutation and the absolute-95 caution remains.
Row 46142 remains 0.831 m at 96% result confidence; the result remains the strongest separated example and no coarser raster is substituted.
Row 61522 remains 0.490 m at 96% result confidence; the narrow absolute margin is preserved without point-cloud or 10 m substitution.
The four guarded-recovery receipts remain absent from canonical; no second runner is created and business execution does not resume.
